handsome: 'High accuracy' cannot be checked, and accuracy is the wrong boast: predicting that everyone stays is 86.8% accurate.
The summary says all 200 of the top 200 churned; the tile beside it says 136. The sentence was typed around an earlier, leaky run and never updated.
No baseline, no interval, and no word on which rows the results come from.
'Reduces churn by 11 points' is a causal verb on an observed gap. Adjusted, the gap is 6.5 points; in this simulated world the true effect is 2.3.
'Rose sharply ... growing dissatisfaction' explains a change of +4.9 points whose interval runs from -1.7 to +11.4: it may not exist.
The recommendation promises 11 points per account from a practice nobody has tested.
Nothing says what not to conclude, and nothing is cut by segment.
